# nycosm ![nycosm package hex logo](reference/figures/nycosm.png)

The nycosm package provides
[OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org) (OSM) features for New
York City, from the Geofabrik extract of 18 October 2026: points of
interest, streets and paths, rail, buildings, land use, parks, water,
and transit routes, with all their OSM tags. There are about 2.5 million
features in five layers. They are stored as GeoParquet files in
EPSG:2263 and accessed via [duckplyr](https://duckplyr.tidyverse.org),
so you read only the rows and columns you need.

Map data © [OpenStreetMap
contributors](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright), available under
the [Open Database License (ODbL)
1.0](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/). The bundled data
are a database derived from OSM and are also under the ODbL. The package
code is MIT licensed.

## Installation

You can install the development version of nycosm from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("kjhealy/nycosm")
```

## Load the package

``` r

library(nycosm)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## What’s included

Each layer has its own function, returning a lazy data frame. Use dplyr
verbs to query it,
[`collect()`](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/compute.html) to
bring results into R, and
[`nyc_osm_to_sf()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm_to_sf.md)
to get an sf object. Every function takes a `borough` argument.

| Function | Features | Rows |
|----|----|----|
| [`nyc_osm_points()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md) | Points of interest, transit stops, crossings, street furniture, trees | 701,481 |
| [`nyc_osm_lines()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md) | Streets, footways, cycleways, rail, waterways, barriers | 471,643 |
| [`nyc_osm_buildings()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md) | Buildings | 1,089,132 |
| [`nyc_osm_areas()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md) | Land use, parks, leisure, water, natural features, amenity areas | 202,990 |
| [`nyc_osm_routes()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md) | Bus, subway, train, ferry, bicycle, and hiking routes | 2,426 |

``` r

nyc_osm_points() |>
  select(-geometry)
#> # A duckplyr data frame: 34 variables
#>    osm_type  osm_id name  amenity shop  cuisine highway public_transport railway
#>    <chr>      <dbl> <chr> <chr>   <chr> <chr>   <chr>   <chr>            <chr>  
#>  1 node     1.20e10 <NA>  waste_… <NA>  <NA>    <NA>    <NA>             <NA>   
#>  2 node     1.13e10 Aaka… <NA>    <NA>  <NA>    <NA>    <NA>             <NA>   
#>  3 node     1.20e10 <NA>  vendin… <NA>  <NA>    <NA>    <NA>             <NA>   
#>  4 node     1.06e10 <NA>  <NA>    <NA>  <NA>    <NA>    <NA>             <NA>   
#>  5 node     1.20e10 <NA>  waste_… <NA>  <NA>    <NA>    <NA>             <NA>

#> #   wikidata <chr>, tags <list>, borough <chr>, osm_extract <date>
```

Common tags are columns. The `tags` column has every OSM tag of each
feature;
[`nyc_osm_add_tags()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm_add_tags.md)
pulls any of them out into columns.

``` r

nyc_osm_points(borough = "Brooklyn") |>
  filter(amenity == "cafe") |>
  nyc_osm_add_tags(c("outdoor_seating", "internet_access")) |>
  count(outdoor_seating, internet_access) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 38 × 3
#>    outdoor_seating internet_access     n
#>  * <chr>           <chr>           <int>
#>  1 <NA>            <NA>              414
#>  2 yes             <NA>               75
#>  3 sidewalk        <NA>               61
#>  4 <NA>            wlan               60
#>  5 no              <NA>               51
#>  6 yes             wlan               17
#>  7 no              wlan               16
#>  8 sidewalk        wlan               11
#>  9 sidewalk;street <NA>               11
#> 10 <NA>            yes                10
#> # ℹ 28 more rows
```

## Example: what’s on the map

``` r

nyc_osm_points() |>
  filter(!is.na(amenity), !is.na(borough)) |>
  count(borough, amenity) |>
  collect() |>
  filter(amenity %in% c("restaurant", "cafe", "bar", "fast_food", "pharmacy")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = amenity, values_from = n)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   borough         bar  cafe fast_food pharmacy restaurant
#>   <chr>         <int> <int>     <int>    <int>      <int>
#> 1 Bronx            23    30       174       55        221
#> 2 Brooklyn        463   802      1433      279       1729
#> 3 Manhattan       662  1242      1539      295       3426
#> 4 Queens          235   412      1125      351       1830
#> 5 Staten Island    24    64       247       94        443
```

## Example: a map

Parks, cycleways, and cafés in lower Manhattan.

``` r

library(sf)

parks <- nyc_osm_areas(borough = "Manhattan") |>
  filter(leisure == "park") |>
  collect() |>
  nyc_osm_to_sf()

buildings <- nyc_osm_buildings(borough = "Manhattan") |>
  select(osm_id, geometry) |>
  collect() |>
  nyc_osm_to_sf()

cycleways <- nyc_osm_lines(borough = "Manhattan") |>
  filter(highway == "cycleway" | cycleway %in% c("lane", "track")) |>
  collect() |>
  nyc_osm_to_sf()

cafes <- nyc_osm_points(borough = "Manhattan") |>
  filter(amenity == "cafe") |>
  collect() |>
  nyc_osm_to_sf()

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = buildings, fill = "gray85", color = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = parks, fill = "#7fbf7b", color = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = cycleways, color = "#2166ac", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_sf(data = cafes, color = "#b2182b", size = 0.6) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(978000, 992000),
    ylim = c(191000, 206000),
    crs = 2263,
    datum = NA
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Lower Manhattan: parks, cycleways, and cafés",
    caption = "Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)."
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

![](reference/figures/README-map-1.png)

## OSM and official NYC data

OSM is edited by volunteers. For authoritative building footprints,
streets, and boundaries, use
[nycbuildings](https://github.com/kjhealy/nycbuildings),
[nyclion](https://github.com/kjhealy/nyclion) or
[nycstreets](https://github.com/kjhealy/nycstreets), and
[nycmaps](https://github.com/kjhealy/nycmaps). Most OSM buildings in NYC
were imported from the city’s footprints; their `nycdoitt_bin` column
joins to `bin` in nycbuildings. OSM adds what the city’s files do not
have: points of interest, footways and cycleways, transit stops and
routes, land use, and natural features, along with building types and
names.

## Data source

- Geofabrik, [New York State
  extract](https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/new-york.html)
  `new-york-261018.osm.pbf` (OSM replication timestamp
  2026-10-18T20:25:06Z).
- Clipped to within 500 feet of the borough boundaries in
  [nycmaps](https://github.com/kjhealy/nycmaps).

# Package index

## OSM layers

Lazy tables of OpenStreetMap features for New York City. Map data ©
OpenStreetMap contributors, under the ODbL 1.0.

- [`nyc_osm_points()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md)
  [`nyc_osm_lines()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md)
  [`nyc_osm_buildings()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md)
  [`nyc_osm_areas()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md)
  [`nyc_osm_routes()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm.md)
  : OpenStreetMap layers for New York City

## Helpers

Paths, conversion to sf, and tag extraction.

- [`nyc_osm_path()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm_path.md)
  : Get the file paths to the OSM GeoParquet files
- [`nyc_osm_to_sf()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm_to_sf.md)
  : Convert collected OSM data to an sf object
- [`nyc_osm_add_tags()`](https://kjhealy.github.io/nycosm/reference/nyc_osm_add_tags.md)
  : Add OSM tags as columns
